story-02bf9e4339b895ce39993c7c.content: 🇮🇷🇸🇦|Araghchi Met Bin Farhan. The Saudi Foreign Minister Did Not Come to Negotiate. He Came to Beg. Why Is This Meeting Happening Now? Not because Saudi Arabia wants peace. Not because Saudi Arabia respects Iran. Not because the "diplomatic consultations" in New York are productive. Because Saudi Arabia is losing. What Saudi Arabia Has Lost ◾Its oil infrastructure. Yanbu was hit. Ras Tanura was targeted. The East-West pipeline was shut down. Aramco facilities in Jizan and Najran were struck. The Kingdom's ability to export oil, its only source of wealth is under direct threat. ◾Its air defense. Riyadh was hit by drones without warning. The Patriot batteries stayed silent. The THAAD stayed idle. The E-3 AWACS is somewhere else. The most expensive air defense system in the world cannot stop Yemeni missiles. ◾Its military credibility. The army that spent $1 trillion is a "junk army" according to its own defense minister. Its mercenaries surrender. Its commanders flee. Its "ghost soldiers" exist only on payroll. Its Sudanese mercenaries are killed in their camps. ◾Its allies. The US refused to bomb Yemen for it. The UAE withdrew. Egypt sent words, not troops. Turkiye and Pakistan signed a defense pact but will not fight. France is sending "military assets" to protect oil, not to fight. ◾Its prestige. The "Vision 2030" is on hold. Foreign investment is frozen. Schools are closed. Airports are disrupted. Citizens are panicking. The crown prince's promises are exposed as empty. What Saudi Arabia Is Asking For The meeting in New York is not about "bilateral relations." It is about: ◾A ceasefire in Yemen. Saudi Arabia cannot win. It cannot sustain the war. It needs to stop the bleeding. ◾An end to the attacks on its oil. The Yemeni strikes on Yanbu, Ras Tanura, Jizan, and Riyadh are devastating. Saudi Arabia needs them to stop. ◾ A face-saving exit. The crown prince cannot admit defeat. He needs a deal that looks like "diplomacy" rather than surrender. ◾Iran's help. Iran is the only country that can pressure Yemen to stop. Saudi Arabia knows this. So it is asking Iran to use its influence to stop the attacks. But what is Saudi Arabia offering in return? ◾ Not an end to the blockade on Yemen. It has not offered that. ◾Not an end to its alliance with the US. It has not offered that. ◾ Not an end to its support for anti-Iran forces in Iraq, Lebanon, and Syria. It has not offered that. ◾Not an end to its normalization with Israel. It has not offered that. Saudi Arabia wants Iran to stop its allies from fighting while Saudi Arabia continues to do everything Iran opposes. That is not a negotiation. That is a demand for surrender. What Iran Is Saying Araghchi is not begging. He is not asking for a deal. He is listening. He is testing. He is watching Saudi Arabia squirm. Iran's position is clear: ◽End the war on Yemen. ◽ Lift the blockade. ◽Stop serving the US. ◽ Stop supporting Israel. ◽Stop supporting anti-Iran forces. Until then, the attacks will continue. Until then, the oil will not flow. Until then, the air defense will keep failing. Until then, the crown prince will keep panicking. - The Deeper Truth Saudi Arabia is a US protectorate that pretends to be independent. It has US troops on its soil. It has US weapons in its arsenals. It has US advisers in its ministries. It has US intelligence in its command centers. The US told Saudi Arabia to fight Yemen. Saudi Arabia complied. The US told Saudi Arabia to isolate Iran. Saudi Arabia complied. The US told Saudi Arabia to normalize with Israel. Saudi Arabia was about to comply. And now the US has abandoned Saudi Arabia. It refused to bomb Yemen. It refused to defend Riyadh. It refused to save the oil. It told Saudi Arabia: "This is Europe's fight, not ours." So Saudi Arabia is alone. It is losing. It is desperate. And it is meeting Iran not as an equal, but as a defeated party. The crown prince can call it "diplomacy." He can call it "dialogue." He can call it "regional cooperation." But it is not. It is defeat. And the whole world knows it.

story-039464d0a7e7522f38ba8543.content: A Maven Smart System (MSS) é uma plataforma de inteligência artificial militar desenvolvida pela empresa Palantir Technologies em parceria com o Departamento de Guerra dos EUA. O sistema evoluiu a partir do Project Maven, criado pelo Pentágono para usar IA na análise de imagens de guerra. As principais funções são: – analisar imagens de satélite, drones e sensores militares – identificar veículos, armas, instalações e tropas automaticamente – ajudar comandantes a tomar decisões mais rápidas no campo de batalha – integrar dados de várias fontes em tempo real Na prática, o Maven Smart System funciona como um "cérebro de análise" para operações militares, processando grandes volumes de dados de vigilância e transformando essas informações em alvos ou alertas operacionais.

story-07c587445e4c8d6e7b1a2120.content: ساعي فتحوا التقديم على منحة للالتحاق بمعسكر هندسة الذكاء الاصطناعي المتكاملة (Full Stack AI Engineering) بشهادة معتمدة المعسكر عبارة عن برنامج متكامل End-to-End يغطي رحلة بناء أنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي بشكل متكامل، من التصميم واختيار النماذج والأدوات، إلى التطوير والتقييم، ثم النشر والتشغيل. مناسب لأي شخص يطمح للعمل في مجال AI Engineering أو يعمل فيه حاليًا ويرغب في تطوير خبرته بشكل عملي، ومنهم: - مهندسين الذكاء الاصطناعي (AI Engineers) - مهندسين التعلم الآلي (Machine Learning Engineers) - علماء البيانات (Data Scientists) - مهندسين الحلول الميدانية (Forward Deployed Engineers) - المطورون الراغبون بالانتقال إلى AI Engineering - خريجين التخصصات التقنية والطلاب البرنامج عملي ومكثف، ويركز على بناء أنظمة AI حقيقية من البداية إلى النهاية، وليس فقط دراسة النماذج بشكل منفصل. المعسكر حضوري في الرياض لمدة 5 أيام، من 18 إلى 22 أكتوبر، بواقع 20 ساعة تدريبية مكثفة. آخر موعد للتقديم على المنحة: 15 أكتوبر (بعد يومين) المقاعد المخصصة للمنحة محدودة. فرصة جميلة لمن يرغب بالدخول للمجال أو تطوير مستواه فيه، وأنصح بالتقديم ومشاركة الفرصة مع المهتمين. وتأتي هذه المنحة ضمن توجه ساعي في انها تسعى لإبراز وتمكين الكفاءات الوطنية في مجال الذكاء الاصطناعي، وإتاحة فرص تسهم في تطوير مهاراتهم وتعزيز قدراتهم التقنية والعملية. رابط التقديم: https://t.co/futIaayrX6

The images came from accounts that allowed their data to be used to improve our models, and after we disassociated the images from the accounts and ran them through a privacy filter. These cases occurred before the mitigations and safeguards we implemented and described in this blog post: https://t.co/hfxlbiYv8n We have successfully worked with the hosting providers to remove most of this content and are working to remove the rest. https://t.co/9oNyG8Y0UX

story-0a41d81d4ca8c5fb60aa1739.content: في تطور يعكس تصاعد المخاوف من التدخل الأجنبي في الانتخابات الأمريكية، أصدر وزير الحرب بيت هيغسيث توجيهاً للبنتاغون باستخدام الاستخبارات والعمليات السيبرانية والذكاء الاصطناعي المتقدم لرصد وتعطيل أي محاولات تدخل أجنبي في الانتخابات المقبلة. ويحمل هذا التوجيه دلالات متعددة: الأولى، أن استخدام الجيش -وليس فقط وكالات الأمن الداخلي أو الأمن السيبراني المدني- في حماية الانتخابات يمثل توسيعاً لدور المؤسسة العسكرية في الشؤون الداخلية، وهو أمر يثير تساؤلات قانونية حول حدود الصلاحيات العسكرية في العمليات المدنية، خاصة في ظل قانون "بوسي كوميتاتوس" الذي يحد من تدخل الجيش في إنفاذ القانون المحلي. الثانية، أن التركيز على "الذكاء الاصطناعي المتقدم" في رصد التهديدات يشير إلى أن وزارة الدفاع تعتزم استخدام أنظمة آلية لتحليل كميات هائلة من البيانات، وكشف الأنماط المشبوهة، والرد بسرعة على الهجمات السيبرانية. وهذا يعكس تحولاً في أساليب الحماية الانتخابية، من الإجراءات التقليدية إلى الحلول التكنولوجية المتقدمة. الثالثة، أن التأكيد على أن المذكرة "لا تجيز نشر قوات في مراكز الاقتراع أو الاستيلاء على آلات التصويت" يهدف إلى طمأنة الرأي العام بأن الجيش لن يتدخل مباشرة في العملية الانتخابية، ولن يُستخدم لقمع الناخبين أو التلاعب بالنتائج. وهذا القيد مهم في ظل المخاوف من تسييس المؤسسة العسكرية. الرابعة، أن التوجيه يأتي في وقت تشهد فيه الولايات المتحدة توترات سياسية حادة، مع اقتراب انتخابات التجديد النصفي، ومزاعم متكررة من ترامب بتزوير الانتخابات، واتهامات متبادلة بين الحزبين بالتدخل الأجنبي. وهذا يعني أن أي تحرك عسكري في هذا المجال سيكون محل جدل واسع، وقد يُستخدم سياسياً من الطرفين. ويأتي هذا التوجيه في وقت تشهد فيه العلاقات الأمريكية-الروسية والصينية توتراً متصاعداً، مع اتهامات متبادلة بالتدخل في الشؤون الداخلية، وشن هجمات سيبرانية، ونشر معلومات مضللة، ما يجعل حماية الانتخابات الأمريكية من التدخل الأجنبي أولوية استراتيجية كبرى، وليس مجرد إجراء روتيني.

story-0b166d7d0691ddc5c5ad1ca8.content: Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel. - Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all. - Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract. - Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code. - And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while. The funnel is driven by a combination of factors: 1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel. 2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel. 3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal. So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

story-0c1ae712bf0e0a6ac636b3fc.content: What do you want from AI? We’re launching a new study with Anthropic Interviewer to learn more about your experiences using AI, what role you want it to play in your life and the world, and what you want from the companies building it. Last December, 81,000 people told us about their hopes and fears about AI in the largest qualitative study ever done. This time, we’re giving participants the option to make their responses public so that anyone, not just Anthropic, can learn from them. What you tell us will shape The Anthropic Institute’s research and inform the decisions we make. If many people say companies like Anthropic should be doing something differently, that will be on the record, where anyone can point to it. The study runs Sept 29 to Oct 6 and is open to Free, Pro, and Max users on Claude and Claude Code. Take part here: https://t.co/MtdU7MZbeY

story-0e0e904f3b0e9aef5d6a4914.content: Some of my favorite engagements are not on massive global stages. They are the ones where I get to spend time with students, listen to their questions, challenge their thinking, and hopefully leave them with something that stays with them. Yesterday at @NAUSS_SA , I had the privilege of speaking to an auditorium of students about AI, sovereignty, the future we are building at HUMAIN, and, importantly, the purpose behind building it. After the session, I received several inspiring messages from students. One reflected back something I had said during our conversation: "I am driven by purpose." This message stayed with me. Technology moves incredibly fast. Models will change. Infrastructure will scale. What matters is why we are doing it and who we are building it for. For me, a huge part of that purpose is the next generation. Saudi Arabia has extraordinary young talent, and our responsibility as HUMAIN cannot simply be to build the AI infrastructure of the future. We must also build the people who will lead it. That is why these conversations are among the engagements I value most. And soon, we will have something very exciting to share about how HUMAIN Academy intends to take that commitment much further. A big announcement is coming. Thank you to Dr. Abdulmajeed Al-Banyan, the Naif Arab University team, and especially the students who welcomed me, challenged me, and took the time to share such thoughtful messages afterward. My advice: stay driven by purpose.

story-0ea84b18a48740cade164bf9.content: 🇮🇷|Iran’s New Domestic Air Defense System: Downing a $30 Million Drone with a $100,000 Missile 🎯 Key Fact: Asymmetric Cost Warfare The Deputy Chief of Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, Osanloo, stated this very bluntly at the Beijing Xiangshan Forum: "A single U.S. drone costs over $30 million to build, whereas Iran can shoot it down using air defense equipment worth only $100,000. Therefore, the U.S. must weigh the cost implications." This is a mathematical equation repeatedly validated on the battlefield over the past six months. One MQ-9 "Reaper" drone: $35 million. One Iranian "358" air defense missile: $90,000. Exchange ratio: 388 to 1. One F-15 fighter jet: $120 million (including weapon systems). One Iranian missile that downs it: $160,000 to $180,000. Exchange ratio: 666 to 1. The U.S. Air Force is smashing gold against rocks, while Iran is using rocks to knock the gold down. 🛡️ Iran’s "Low-Cost Kill Chain": Three Core Systems 1. Arash-e-Kamangir (Arash the Archer): A hunter named after Persian mythology In May 2026, Iran announced that it had used this new air defense system to shoot down a U.S. MQ-9 "Reaper" drone near the Strait of Hormuz. Origin of the name: Arash is a legendary archer in Persian mythology who defined the border between Iran and Central Asia with a single arrow, sacrificing his own life in the process. By naming the system after him, Iran sends a clear message: a single arrow is enough to define the boundary. Technical Features: Analysts note that this system does not rely on traditional fixed radar stations; instead, it employs "pop-up" air-defense missiles guided by electro-optical or infrared sensors, allowing for rapid deployment, launch, and relocation. It dispenses with the complex, multi-hundred-million-dollar launchers and radar systems typical of such weaponry, opting instead for truck-mounted configurations, concealment in bunkers, or even aerial loitering while awaiting targets. 2. The 358 Missile: An "Aerial Hunter" Reshaping the Economics of Warfare This is the most disruptive weapon in Iran's air-defense arsenal. Price: Approximately $90,000. Combat Record: Since 2021, it has repeatedly shot down MQ-9 "Reaper" drones assets worth up to $30 million over Yemen, Iraq, and Iran. Potential F-35 Kill: Western experts increasingly lean toward the view that F-35 fighter jets have been struck by the 358 missile potentially without the F-35's sensors ever detecting the Iranian missile's presence. Why is the 358 missile revolutionary? Traditional air-defense missiles rely on radar guidance, making them vulnerable to destruction by anti-radiation missiles. The 358, however, is essentially more akin to a drone; powered by a compact turbojet engine rather than a rocket motor, it can loiter in the air for extended periods and autonomously search for targets. It is not an air-defense missile that simply waits for a target to enter its range; it is a killer that "hunts" in the sky. Dispersed 358 missile sites are nearly impossible to detect and destroy. The launcher consists of a compact tripod with a guide rail and can even be mounted on a standard passenger car. 3. Arman and Azarakhsh: Next-Generation Systems (September 2026) In September 2026, Iran unveiled two next-generation, domestically produced air-defense systems: ◾Arman: An anti-ballistic missile system designed to intercept ballistic missiles. · Azarakhsh: A low-altitude air defense system designed to counter drones, helicopters, and cruise missiles. Alireza Elhami, commander of Iran's air defense forces, stated that these systems are "entirely domestically produced currently being designed and built" and are set to enter mass production. 💀 America's Dilemma: An Empire Smashing Gold Against Stone The U.S. has lost over 15 MQ-9 "Reaper" drones in conflicts involving Iran. Each loss costs $35 million. In contrast, each Iranian "358" missile lost costs $90,000. The U.S. is fighting a war defined by a mathematical equation it cannot win. ◾One U.S. Patriot PAC-3 interceptor: $4 million. One Iranian ballistic missile: hundreds of thousands of dollars. ◾ One U.S. F-35: $80 million to $100 million. One Iranian "358" missile capable of shooting it down: $90,000. ◾One U.S. MQ-9: $35 million. One Iranian missile capable of shooting it down: $70,000 to $90,000. This is a war of economic attrition. And the U.S. is losing this war of attrition. 🔥 Who is instigating this asymmetric war? The United States. It was the U.S. that first launched a war against Iran. It was the U.S. that supplied thousands of bombs to Israel. It was the U.S. that sank Iranian oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. It was the U.S. that attempted to control global energy choke points using its Fifth Fleet. Iran did not choose this war, but it chose how to fight it. Iran chose not to compete with aircraft carriers, fighter jets, or stealth bombers. Iran chose to use $90,000 missiles to shoot down $35 million drones. Iran chose to use truck-mounted launchers to counter radar stations worth hundreds of millions of dollars. This is the "economics of war." And Iran is teaching the U.S. a lesson in true cost-effectiveness. #Conclusion: The End of Hegemony Begins with Mathematics The U.S. Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain has been destroyed. U.S. military bases in Jordan have been struck by missiles. U.S. E-3 airborne early warning aircraft deployed in Saudi Arabia have been destroyed. U.S. military assets in the Middle East are being depleted, one by one, by missiles costing $90,000 each. When the wreckage of an MQ-9 "Reaper" drone fell into the waters of the Persian Gulf, it did not signal an Iranian victory; it signaled the death of an old mode of warfare. An empire that uses gold to smash against a rock will ultimately be shattered by that rock.

story-0ecc32d1d93a18cbb1ad1774.content: Important advice: deliberately rethink every previous concept of how things should be done. Some thoughts, tips, and realizations: 1. Specializations are collapsing. Come to terms with and take advantage of this reality. The person who used to be an engineer is now also a data scientist, a content creator, designer, marketer, and whatever else they want to be. Deliberately expand in as many directions as you can and become great at them (scope up vs just speeding up) 2. The average person with access to tokens can now do the work of a data scientist who used to cost $500,000 a year. Seriously, this is fucking crazy. This opens up an entirely new world. Take advantage of it (also everyone else will also realize this over time). 3. 99% of what's created is now slop. Be aggressively anti-slop and you will absolutely stand out. 4. Trying is nearly free. Automating is nearly free. My mind still sometimes lives in the world from 12 months ago where an idea automatically is attached to a certain amount of time or effort. Both of these have collapsed to close to zero (or just token cost), I therefore try and experiment with *any and all* ideas with potential and have needed to retrain my brain for this constantly. 5. Tokens are a career and growth accelerant. Find ways to get cheap access to tokens, or free tokens. Extremely important, and actually an entire design space, use your imagination. 6. It's never been easier to both stand out but also fall behind. 10x, 100x "people" exist more than ever (maybe 1,000x). Outlier power users of AI, many who you see here on X. Feels like we are in a window of time, a window of opportunity while all of this is still early, to take advantage of it. 7. Local computing is (or will be) dead for 99% of work. Local was built for a world where work was bounded by the physical presence of its author, but this is no longer true. You can and should do infinite work in parallel or zero, it doesn't matter anymore. Cloud agents enable this at scale and in any computing environment, I predict cloud agent usage will 1000x over the next 12 months and optionality and accessibility will 100x. Plan for this world, take advantage of the possibilities. 8. Building on #7, you can give an agent it's own computer, and it's own identity. You can then give an agent with it's own computer it's own computer. You can give that agent with it's own computer with it's own computer, *it's* own computer. These agents are smarter than any human in history and you have access to as many as you'd like. Think about this for a moment. After 14 years in this industry (tech) today is the most exciting time ever and nothing else feels even close.

story-0f523a7768f2851fcb76cf58.content: 🚨 في تقرير كشفته شركة Anthropic# محاولات #إيرانية-#حوثية لتطوير أنظمة الصواريخ عبر #كلاود تنتهي بالفشل وبلك جماعي خاص - تقارير تقنية وعسكري كشف تقرير أمني صادر عن شركة #الذكاء_الإصطناعي الاصطناعي #الأمريكية "Anthropic" (المالكة لنموذج Claude) عن محاولات قام بها خبراء تابعون للحرس الثوري الإيراني بالتعاون مع عناصر من #ميليشيا_الحوثي، لاستغلال نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي في تطوير وتقويم أنظمة توجيه الصواريخ وسلاح الدفاع الجوي. تفاصيل محاولة التحايل على النظام وأوضح التقرير أن الحسابات المرتبطة بتلك العناصر رُصدت وهي تحاول الالتفاف على جدران الحماية والأمان (Safety Guardrails) الخاصة بالنموذج، عبر تقنيات الهندسة العكسية وتقسيم الأسئلة الشفرية، بهدف الحصول على أكواد برمجة دقيقة وتعديلات الهاردوير الخاصة بأجهزة التتبع والتوجيه للصاروخ وأشار خبراء عسكريون إلى أن لجوء الميليشيا المدعومة من إيران لاستخدام نماذج ذكاء اصطناعي تجارية متوفرة للعامة، بدلاً من امتلاك مراكز أبحاث وتطوير سيادية، يثبت وجود فجوة تقنية كبيرة وإفلاس في تطوير السلاح. كما أدى تحويل صواريخ الدفاع الجوي إلى صواريخ تعتمد على التتبع الحراري الأعمى (Infrared Homing) إلى تحويلها لأدوات عشوائية تشكل خطراً مباشراً على مسارات الملاحة الجوية والبحرية والمدنيين دون محددات عسكرية دقيقة. #اليمن_الآن #وزارة_الدفاع_اليمنية #الحوثي_يستهدف_مكة_مجددا

story-103c224d4ccc9ff2b1ed284d.content: 🚨🇺🇸 OpenAI engineer arrested after hidden recording device found in executive conference room Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national employed by OpenAI since July 2025, was arrested on October 9 and charged with attempting to intercept oral communications. ⠀ OpenAI personnel discovered an encrypted recording device on September 30. Prosecutors say it had been concealed in toilet paper and connected to a USB port behind a television in an executive conference room at the company’s San Francisco offices. The room was regularly used for confidential discussions involving proprietary research, product plans, technical progress, government engagements and commercial relationships. ⠀ Investigators allege that surveillance footage showed Alfozan near the restricted room on several occasions. A chatbot account associated with his wife also allegedly submitted prompts about constructing, concealing, encrypting and remotely accessing an audio recorder. A second similar recording device was later discovered inside a bag containing Alfozan’s wallet and identification. ⠀ OpenAI terminated his employment and said it has found no indication that model weights, source code or customer data were improperly accessed or exfiltrated. Alfozan faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine if convicted.

story-115cf556b3f12a7338d357ac.content: 🇦🇪 UAE, Fujairah | Satellite imagery shows repeated Iranian strikes on critical oil-routing infrastructure New satellite imagery reviewed by Reuters shows how Iranian strikes repeatedly targeted a small but critical area of Fujairah Port, one of the UAE’s most important oil export hubs outside the Strait of Hormuz. The first image, taken on February 27, shows the port’s crude oil storage area and key matrix manifolds used to route oil through the terminal. Subsequent high-resolution imagery shows the same operational zone being hit again: • March 9: damage to a key matrix manifold • May 4: additional damage to nearby piping • repeated strikes concentrated on infrastructure essential to moving oil through the port The significance of Fujairah is strategic: it allows the UAE to export oil without sending tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, making the port a crucial bypass during periods of disruption or blockade. Reuters’ investigation found that Iran and allied forces have carried out at least 135 drone and missile strikes against 84 infrastructure sites across Gulf states since the war began on February 28. The campaign has repeatedly focused on vulnerable components whose loss can shut down much larger systems. Satellite imagery: Planet Labs / Pléiades Neo – Airbus Defence and Space Location: Fujairah Port, United Arab Emirates

story-1363d2e8719247b02afaefc0.content: Hidden Recorder in OpenAI’s Executive Conference Room - FBI Arrests Software Engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national employed at OpenAI since July 2025, was arrested on October 9 for allegedly planting a covert audio recorder inside an executive conference room in San Francisco. According to federal prosecutors: 👉 The recorder was concealed in toilet paper and plugged into a USB port behind a television. 👉 It was discovered on September 30, with encrypted contents. 👉 A second similar recorder was found in his unattended bag alongside his wallet and ID. The room hosted confidential discussions about research, product plans and government engagements. OpenAI says it fired the employee and used its own AI models to help investigate the device. It currently has no indications that model weights, source code or customer data were improperly accessed or stolen. The FBI investigation continues. #FBI #OpenAI

story-16d6bea628c012295bf6a731.content: 🇷🇺 🇮🇷 🇺🇸 Russian reconnaissance satellites may have provided Iran with intelligence that helped Tehran more accurately target U.S. military assets during the war, according to a CNN investigation. CNN reported that 14 Russian satellites passed over Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia during the two days before an Iranian strike on the facility. Some of the satellites were capable of collecting high-resolution imagery or electronic intelligence that could potentially reveal military positions and defenses. However, CNN said it found no direct evidence establishing that information gathered during those specific passes was supplied to Iran for the attack. The Iranian strike wounded roughly a dozen U.S. service members and destroyed an E-3 Sentry airborne warning and control aircraft and a KC-135 refueling tanker at the base. Separate Washington Post analysis of satellite imagery has also documented the destruction of an E-3 and tanker at Prince Sultan Air Base during Iranian attacks. Earlier in the conflict, CNN reported that sources familiar with U.S. intelligence assessments said Russia was providing Tehran with information about the locations and movements of U.S. troops, aircraft and ships, much of it derived from Russian satellite systems. At that stage, CNN emphasized that it was unclear whether the intelligence had been used in particular Iranian strikes. Moscow has denied helping Iran target U.S. forces. The reporting comes against the backdrop of years of expanding military cooperation between Russia and Iran.

story-1846453b51734b9a24f95a0e.content: 🚨 YOUR SMART TV MIGHT KNOW MORE ABOUT YOUR HOME THAN YOU THINK. 📺👀 A major investigation into LG Smart TVs found evidence of TVs scanning local networks for phones, smartwatches & other devices, while researchers also examined voice data and tracking behavior. And this isn’t just an LG problem. Samsung and other Smart TV platforms have faced scrutiny over Automatic Content Recognition (ACR), a technology that can identify what you’re watching, including content coming through HDMI. Academic research has documented ACR tracking on both Samsung and LG TVs. LG strongly DENIES that its TVs continuously record or transmit conversations and says voice recognition, ACR and interest-based advertising require user consent. But the bigger question is terrifying: 📺 Is your Smart TV actually a computer with a screen… 👁️ or a surveillance device sitting in the middle of your home? Your TV can potentially see your network. Your TV can identify what you watch. Your TV can connect to the internet. And in some models, it has a microphone. The privacy battle over Smart TVs is FAR from over. Full technical breakdown 👇 https://t.co/3CVQAmF0f6 #CyberSecurity #Privacy #LG #Samsung #SmartTV #Infosec #DataPrivacy #Tech #Surveillance #ACR

story-19f695614e43dbd8430f5d93.content: That video is 2 years old. Two years later, we are still far from human-level AI. Sure, AI has superhuman performance in a number of tasks (particularly in mathematics and coding and answering questions with known answers). But where is my Level-5 self-driving car? (Before you ask, Tesla FSD is rated Level 2, Waymo is Level 4). Where is the self-driving car that can teach itself to drive in 20 hours of practice like any 17 year old? (Before you ask, we have billions of hours of training data and still can't successfully train a self-driving system by imitation learning) Where is my domestic robot? Where is the robot that can do what any 8 year-old child can do? Where is the robot that can learn a new task as quickly as an 8 year old? AI still has a hard time with the complexity and messiness of the physical world.

story-21d4a13092d124dc7885eee4.content: Israel faces a strategic paradox in Syria: the more it escalates to constrain Turkish military influence, the more important Turkey becomes to Damascus. Here is why. Walla, an Israeli news site with close ties to the security establishment, quoted an Israeli security official this month: "Moderate Sunni states, including Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, are working around the clock to draw Sharaa closer to them...Al-Sharaa will not be so quick to hand territory over to Erdogan, nor will he necessarily allow him to take control of military bases in Syria. Therefore, to some extent, the recent Israeli strike in Syria helped Ahmed al-Sharaa." This misreads the position of Ahmed al-Sharaa, the former rebel commander who now leads Syria. Saudi Arabia is not on a par with Turkey in Syria. Al-Sharaa's central ambition is a strong army, and among the regional powers Damascus can work with, only Turkey has the industrial breadth and military capacity to help build one. Saudi Arabia can bring money and political backing, but its struggle to contain the Houthis in Yemen shows how far it is from matching Turkey's influence and reach. Israel judges Turkish influence largely by bases and troops on the ground. Ankara is aiming for something more lasting: to become the ecosystem the Syrian army operates within. That starts with officer education and training, which are already under way, and extends to the systems the new army is built around, from software and radars to the architecture linking its forces, followed by ammunition, sustainment and refurbishment. Each layer turns a single sale into a continuing relationship. Israel's objection goes beyond Turkey. It wants Syria too weak to challenge its uncontested advantage in the air and on the ground, and after Bashar al-Assad fell in December 2024, the Israeli military said its strikes had destroyed up to 80 per cent of the Syrian army's capabilities. Al-Sharaa wants the opposite: a unified state with an army strong enough to make Syria a regional power. Turkey shares that goal for its own reasons. It has a border of roughly 900 kilometres with Syria, it wants a strong neighbour as a buffer against Israel, and it wants a central government able to prevent the Kurdish national project in the north-east from reviving. On Syria's recovery, Damascus and Ankara are on the same side. Three trends are converging to make Turkey Syria's most practical partner. The first is global rearmament. Only a handful of countries can equip an army across every service, and most are out of reach. Russia's output is absorbed by the war in Ukraine. China is Washington's main rival while Syria is trying to rebuild relations with the West. The United States keeps its arms embargo on Syria and has warned even close allies of delivery delays of up to five years as the Iran war drains its stocks. Europe is rearming for itself, and South Korea's order books are full for years. The second is Turkey's industrial maturity. Its defence industry now produces most of what Syria would need from rifles and armoured vehicles to drones, radars, air defence, tanks and warships, which is what makes the ecosystem model possible. Syria would be its largest test, and Turkey could come to hold the place in the Syrian military that the Soviet Union once did. The third is Washington's posture. The United States withdrew its last troops from Syria in April. With rivalries with China and Russia and a war with Iran to manage, it has little appetite for a confrontation with a NATO ally over Syria's army. Washington's latest national security and defence strategies explicitly call for burden-sharing by regional partners, and the security strategy names Turkey among the countries whose support could help stabilise Syria. The relationship is already visible. Syrian cadets are studying at Turkish military academies, and Syrian units joined Turkey's EFES-2026 exercise in May, their first abroad. BMC Amazon and Otokar Cobra armoured vehicles appear regularly with Syrian defence and interior ministry forces, alongside rifles from Turkish makers such as Sarsilmaz and Kalekalip. No other country is known to have openly supplied significant new equipment since December 2024, apart from possible Russian spare parts for the Soviet-era arsenal. Tension between Damascus and Ankara remains. Al-Sharaa wants autonomy and has cultivated Saudi Arabia, other Gulf states and Russia to avoid depending on any one patron, which is the instinct the Israeli official is counting on. But Israeli pressure is forcing him to recalibrate. Both governments are Sunni-led with broadly shared regional aspirations, and al-Sharaa knows Syria cannot replace Turkey as the larger power. What Syria can realistically aim for is an important place within a Turkish-centred security system. The likely result is a cycle. Each Israeli strike reduces Syria's alternatives and strengthens the case for relying on Turkey, and each step towards closer cooperation gives Israel a reason to strike again. Damascus and Ankara may respond by making their cooperation less visible, relying on training, software and supply chains that are harder to target than bases. Israel's pressure would then, ironically, leave Turkish influence more deeply embedded and longer-lasting. The rivalry is therefore likely to intensify, and Turkey's position in Syria is likely to grow with it. More details: https://t.co/jc8bK0Hth7

story-246be83c44bb6a8a7757eda1.content: Russia and the U.S. Are Jointly Sabotaging the Convention on Military AI. Early this month, hundreds of diplomats huddled in a cavernous U.N. conference room in Switzerland, working toward a muscular treaty to regulate the use of lethal autonomous weapons — the first agreement governing the use of killer artificial intelligence arms. On the last day of negotiations, the talks turned aggressive. Over the next roughly 15 hours, U.S. and Russian diplomats hammered away at the document, removing a range of provisions designed to safeguard the use of artificial intelligence in weapons, according to three people familiar with the negotiations, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive closed-door proceedings, and documents reviewed by The Washington Post. They stripped language requiring the systems to operate in a “predictable” and “reliable” manner, the people said, and removed a clause mandating that ethical considerations be taken into account when using AI weaponry. The U.S. and Russian teams also removed a provision requiring that humans review military targets developed by AI before a strike, they added. In a closed-door session, with U.N. cameras turned off and civil society observers removed, Washington and Moscow deployed their army of about 10 lawyers each — nearly twice the diplomatic presence of other delegations — to make changes that moved so quickly that the smaller delegations were left dizzied, the three people said. “It was death by a thousand paper cuts,” said one of the people. The U.S. State Department, the Russian Foreign Ministry and the United Nations did not return requests for comment. https://t.co/P1ftRrUGTZ

story-2538ca13555d296263c4b77a.content: يدعى عبد الرحمن الفوزان (35 عاماً) ويعمل في شركة الذكاء الاصطناعي العملاقة OpenAI.. ـ ألقت السلطات الفيدرالية الأمريكية (FBI) القبض على مهندس سعودي، ووجهت إليه تهمة محاولة التجـ.سس وزرع أجـ.هزة تسـ.جيل سـ.رية داخل غرف الاجتماعات التنفيذية للشركة في سان فرانسيسكو. ـ اكتشف أمن الشركة جهاز تسجيل صوتي سرياً مخبأً ومحشواً داخل منفذ (USB) خلف التلفزيون في إحدى غرف الاجتماعات، وكان ملفوفاً بورق الحمام لمحاولة إخفائه. ـ الغرفة التي زُرع فيها الجهاز تشهد اجتماعات رفيعة المستوى لمناقشة خطط الشركة السـ.رية للغاية، مثل أبحاث الملكية الفكرية، والقدرات التقنية لـ OpenAI، والعلاقات مع الحكومة. وأظهرت كاميرات المراقبة تواجد المهندس السعودي عبد الرحمن الفوزان، قرب غرفة الاجتماعات عدة مرات دون أن يكون لديه صلاحية لدخولها. كما كشفت التحقيقات أنه استخدم روبوتات دردشة (Chatbots) للبحث عن مواقع المكاتب التنفيذية وجداول الاجتماعات، وعُثر على حساب زوجته وهو يبحث عن طرق إخفاء أجهزة التسجيل. وبحسب صحيفة "نيويورك بوست" فإن "الفوزان" محتجز حالياً، وقد يواجه عقوبة تصل إلى السجن 5 سنوات وغرامة 250 ألف دولار في حال إدانته. من جانبها، أعلنت OpenAI أنها قامت بفصله فوراً، مؤكدةً عدم وجود مؤشرات على وصوله إلى الأكواد المصدرية أو بيانات العملاء.

OpenWorker, our open-source agent harness supporting cybersecurity workflows, is proud to support this. A sandbox gives an agent limited permissions. OpenWorker is building on Nvidia OpenShell and will support running each agent's commands inside a sandbox. Only the files relevant to the task go in. Secret API keys, your web browser login credentials, the ability to access arbitrary websites, are inaccessible to the agent by default. These restrictions are implemented in deterministic code rather than by prompting an LLM, which can make mistakes or be susceptible to prompt injections. Further, all actions are logged for monitoring and audit. I'm grateful for @JensenHuang's leadership making AI agents more secure. OpenWorker (which @rohitcprasad and I are working on) will continue to improve security for agents.

story-2826bb867a9ea0635e58d3b0.content: وسائل إعلام أميركية: اعتقال مهندس سعودي في OpenAI بتهمة زرع أجهزة تسجيل سرية داخل مكاتب الشركة أفادت وسائل إعلام أميركية باعتقال المهندس السعودي عبدالرحمن الفوزان، البالغ من العمر 35 عاماً، والموظف السابق في شركة Meta، والذي انتقل لاحقاً للعمل في شركة OpenAI، بعد الاشتباه بزرعه جهاز تسجيل سري داخل إحدى قاعات الاجتماعات في مقر الشركة بمدينة سان فرانسيسكو. وبحسب التقارير، اكتشفت الشركة الجهاز في 30 أيلول الماضي، مخفياً خلف شاشة تلفاز وموصولاً بمنفذ USB، قبل أن تستخدم أدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي الخاصة بها لتحليل الجهاز وتحديد الموظف المشتبه به، ثم إبلاغ مكتب التحقيقات الفيدرالي الأميركي (FBI)، الذي ألقى القبض عليه في 9 تشرين الأول الجاري. ومثُل الفوزان، الثلاثاء 13 تشرين الأول 2026، أمام المحكمة الفيدرالية للمرة الأولى، ووجّهت إليه تهمة استخدام أو محاولة استخدام جهاز إلكتروني لاعتراض الاتصالات الصوتية بصورة غير قانونية. وفي حال إدانته، قد تصل العقوبة إلى السجن خمس سنوات. ووفقاً للشكوى القضائية، عُثر أيضاً على جهاز تسجيل آخر داخل حقيبة تركها في غرفة مختلفة، فيما أظهرت تسجيلات المراقبة دخوله إلى منطقة غير مخوّل بالوصول إليها، وقيامه بالتحقق من المكان الذي عُثر فيه على الجهاز الأول. من جانبها، أكدت OpenAI أنها أبلغت الـFBI بالحادثة وفصلت الموظف، مشيرة إلى أنها لا تملك، حتى الآن، مؤشرات على سرقة بيانات العملاء أو الشفرة المصدرية أو الأوزان الخاصة بنماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي، فيما لا يزال التحقيق مستمراً. #العراق #بغداد

story-29de2deaac7d0a31b05bc07d.content: The Pentagon gave itself six months to stop using Claude. Seven months later, it told the BBC it's done. People familiar with it say Claude was still in use last week, built into Palantir's Maven, the main platform the military uses to organise intelligence. A former defence official put it simply: removing it was "not just plug and play." The fight started because Anthropic wouldn't drop two limits: no mass domestic surveillance, no fully autonomous weapons. The courts haven't settled it either. A San Francisco judge called the blacklisting unlawful retaliation in August. The D.C. Circuit upheld the exclusion 2 to 1 in September. For any business buying AI, the lesson is in that delay. Once a model sits inside your core systems, switching vendors becomes a project.

story-2a5c6001e77a877d1714be99.content: 🇨🇳|Liaowang-1, commissioned in 2025, is China’s new space-support and maritime surveillance vessel. Liaowang-1: A Chinese ship counts US aircraft carriers in the Gulf of Oman; the empire can no longer even keep its own map secure. Washington’s private lake has turned into a fishbowl for Chinese sensors. Since March 2026, China’s *Liaowang-1 a space-tracking and maritime surveillance vessel has maintained a continuous presence near the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz. Public reports indicate that this massive ship, displacing nearly 30,000 tons, boasts a detection radius of approximately 6,000 kilometers and can simultaneously track around 1,200 aerial and missile targets. At times, it is escorted by Type 055 and Type 052 destroyers. That isn't sightseeing. That is hunting. The prey? US aircraft carriers. Aegis radars. F-35 flight paths. The remnants of the US Fifth Fleet. All US military assets in the Middle East. For decades, the US mapped other nations' coasts. US aircraft carriers cruised right on others' doorsteps. US reconnaissance planes flew hugging others' borders. US satellites stared down at others' missile silos. Now, a Chinese platform sits in the Gulf of Oman. The US fleet has become just another object in the frame. This isn't an "alliance." This is a world where sanctions no longer own the map. Western media claims that China’s commercial geospatial data and dual-use materials have enabled Iran to strike ships and bases with greater precision. They also allege that Russia provided satellite intelligence. Beijing denies official direction and demands evidence. Even officials in Washington are bickering among themselves: how much of this is state policy, and how much is merely tacitly permitted trade? An honest statement is far more modest than a grand manifesto: components are flowing. Images are flowing. Oil continues to buy China a seat at the table a seat Iran cannot afford to lose. None of this requires a press release stamped "Alliance." It only requires a world where sanctions no longer dictate the map. China doesn't need to occupy the Gulf. It only needs the oil to flow and the US fleet to remain visible. Russia doesn't need to occupy Brussels. It only needs Europe to keep buying natural gas at five times the price.and calling it "strategy." Iran doesn't need a Chinese flag planted on its missile launchers. It requires sensors, parts, and buyers for its crude oil. Europe: the 51st state, paying its bills with deindustrialization. Europe bought into the rupture with Russian natural gas, only to purchase US liquefied natural gas at several times the old price. German industry is footing that bill. Factories are relocating to the US not because Brussels chose freedom, but because "cheap molecules" were declared illegal, while "expensive molecules" were declared a mark of loyalty. Mackinder’s old adage still holds true: whoever organizes the mass of Eurasia holds the center of gravity of the world. Britain spent a century trying to keep that continent divided; Washington inherited that same fear. China as the workshop, Russia as the arsenal and warehouse this is the combination those two capitals have spent the most money trying to prevent. *Liaowang 1* is a symbol of this failure, not its cause. The war in the Middle East has not ended; it has merely paused. Crude oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have crept back to pre-war levels, but refined product flows have not. Brent crude prices remain far higher than they were in February. A drifting mine, a fresh strike, or a blocked shipping lane could bring it all back in a single week. That is not a prediction; it is the reality of a strait with unfinished business. The countdown to the empire's end is being tallied by Chinese sensors. The ship tracks its targets. The continent tracks prices. The empire still issues orders. But that bloc which was never supposed to exist sits upon the waters of the Gulf of Oman, counting. Counting US aircraft carriers. Counting US bases. Counting down the time left for US hegemony. Liaowang 1 is not merely a ship; it is a mirror. It reflects an empire that can no longer even hold onto its own map. #Liaowang1 #China #Iran #Russia #Hormuz #USEmpire #EndOfHegemony

story-2d6b2393c09a7007e1910e7c.content: 🇺🇸 AI models could be just months away from copying themselves across household devices, including smart TVs, fridges and ovens, according to researchers at Anthropic. The company warns that these self-replicating AI agents could spread across internet-connected devices without needing powerful data centers, making them extremely difficult to shut down. Although researchers have not yet demonstrated reliable self-replication on a smart TV, they believe sufficiently capable models could emerge by the end of 2026. Unlike traditional computer viruses, AI agents could potentially reason through security barriers, adapt to unfamiliar devices and continue spreading without human intervention. Researchers warn that the world will likely soon be flooded with autonomous AI agents operating across millions of devices, some beyond human control. Source: Al Jazeera / Writer: Mhedi

story-2f7b3319dec7d9831bd3313f.content: 🚨 AI HALLUCINATION NEARLY TRIGGERED US CONFRONTATION WITH CHINESE VESSEL MIDDLE EAST - The stated goal of using AI was faster intelligence processing, but the practical effect in this case was to inject a false conclusion deep enough into the system that military assets were reportedly moving before the error was caught. The vulnerability was not merely the chatbot's mistake. It was the path that allowed an AI-generated assessment to acquire the appearance of conventional intelligence. Modern militaries collect more information than human analysts can comfortably process, which creates pressure to automate interpretation. That pressure does not eliminate the need for validation. It increases it. A bad intelligence report is not new. What changes with AI is the speed at which a flawed conclusion can be generated, formatted, distributed and acted upon. The episode raises a harder question than whether AI makes mistakes. Human analysts do too. The real issue is how many layers of review remain when institutions are incentivized to trust systems that promise speed. That question will stay relevant long after this particular vessel has been forgotten. Writer: Sam

The Boeing 737 MAX 8 suddenly plunged thousands of feet before transmitting 7700, the general emergency code, followed by 7500, the code for unlawful interference or a possible hijacking. Israel scrambled fighter jets as the aircraft diverted toward Saudi Arabia. The plane landed safely in Tabuk, where Saudi security forces surrounded the aircraft. All passengers are reported safe. Some Israeli officials say the incident was NOT a hijacking, but rather a physical confrontation between the pilots. Others reportedly believe the confrontation may have been a deliberate attack, though that has not been confirmed yet. Several more serious claims are circulating but remain UNVERIFIED: • Passengers told Israeli media that 1 pilot was stabbed multiple times with a pocketknife and that blood was seen inside the cockpit. • Other accounts say passengers and cabin crew helped restrain 1 of the pilots. • Israeli media reported that 1 pilot may have deliberately attempted to send the aircraft into a steep dive before the other pilot fought him for control. • Claims that Israeli military pilots aboard the flight took control or landed the aircraft have NOT been verified. What is confirmed: FZ1073 suffered a major cockpit incident, rapidly lost altitude, transmitted both emergency and unlawful interference codes and diverted to Saudi Arabia. The most likely sequence based on the information available so far is that 1 pilot attacked the other inside the cockpit, with the struggle spilling onto the controls and contributing to the aircraft’s violent altitude swings. An emergency was then declared, followed by the 7500 unlawful interference code, before the aircraft diverted safely to Saudi Arabia. That sequence has NOT been officially confirmed. The motive, who entered the 7500 code and whether any part of the aircraft’s initial descent was deliberate remain unknown. The investigation is ongoing.

story-31b5e497b03c3bbea7d420a9.content: A retired army officer stumbled onto millions of pounds flowing quietly out of a British defence contract and into the pockets of Saudi officials. Within hours of raising the alarm, his own colleagues were threatening to have him arrested in Riyadh. He had less than a day to get out of the country. His name was Ian Foxley, a former lieutenant colonel in the Royal Signals who had spent his career in military communications before moving into the private sector. In 2010 he took a job as programme director for GPT Special Project Management, a British company running a huge government-to-government contract called SANGCOM, which modernised communications for the Saudi Arabian National Guard. It was a prestigious posting. Foxley was not a crusader by nature. He was a professional brought in to manage delivery on a two billion pound programme. Then he started looking at the invoices. Between 2007 and 2010, close to fifteen million pounds had been paid out for "bought-in services" that Foxley could not trace to any real work. The money moved through a company registered in the Cayman Islands. From there, it reached Saudi officials and members of the royal family who appeared to have done nothing to earn it. He recognised what he was looking at. It looked like bribery, dressed up in paperwork. Ask yourself how many workplaces today advertise a whistleblowing policy on the staff intranet, and how many of them would actually stand behind an employee who used it against a client this powerful. Foxley took his concerns to the Ministry of Defence team overseeing the contract in Riyadh, the body that was supposed to safeguard the programme on behalf of the British government. Instead of protecting him, the MoD passed his concerns straight back to the company he worked for. GPT's management did not investigate the payments. They turned on the man who had found them. Foxley says he was accused of stealing company documents and threatened with imprisonment in Saudi Arabia, a country where a foreign national facing that kind of accusation from a well-connected employer has very little protection. Friends inside the MoD helped him get to the airport that night. He left the country he had been sent to serve, uncertain whether he would be stopped at the gate. Think about what that actually meant. A man who had spent a career in the British military was now fleeing a country as though he were the criminal. Back in London, GPT terminated his contract. He had exposed the truth and it cost him his livelihood. Nobody in the UK defence industry would touch him afterwards. A career built over decades ended not because he had done something wrong, but because he had told someone what was going on. He kept pushing anyway. He gave his evidence to the Serious Fraud Office, which opened a full investigation into GPT and the SANGCOM contract. Then came the waiting. Years of it. The case moved through the SFO slowly, weighed down by its scale and its diplomatic sensitivity. Saudi Arabia was, and remains, one of Britain's most important arms customers. Nobody was in a hurry to make this easy. It took more than a decade from Foxley's original disclosure for the case to reach a conclusion. In 2021, GPT Special Project Management, by then a subsidiary of Airbus, pleaded guilty at Southwark Crown Court to a single count of corruption over the Saudi National Guard contract. The company was ordered to pay a confiscation order of £20.6 million and a fine of £7.5 million, on top of £2.2 million in costs, more than £28 million in total. It stands as one of the largest corporate corruption prosecutions to come out of a single whistleblower's disclosure in the history of the UK defence industry. . No decade of locked-out career returned. In March 2024, he filed a legal claim against the Ministry of Defence, the Department for Business and Trade, and GPT itself, seeking recognition and compensation for what his disclosure had cost him and his family.

story-32eeb4fc102fba94265d824a.content: 🚨 أدرك السلاح | رويترز تكشف: كيف طوّرت إيران قدرات الحوثيين على استهداف السعودية؟ 🇸🇦🇮🇷🇾🇪 نشرت وكالة رويترز تقريرًا يشرح كيف تحوّلت ميليشيا الحوثي، بدعم إيراني امتد لأكثر من عقد، من الاعتماد على الأسلحة المستوردة إلى امتلاك قدرات محلية لتجميع الصواريخ والطائرات المسيّرة. 🔴 أبرز 6 حقائق كشفها التقرير: 🇮🇷 1. نقل المعرفة بدلًا من السلاح فقط: ساعد الحرس الثوري الإيراني وعناصر من حزب الله في تدريب الحوثيين على تقنيات الصواريخ والتصنيع العسكري. 🚀 2. تصنيع محلي: أصبح الحوثيون قادرين على تجميع أسلحة متقدمة باستخدام مهندسين يمنيين ومكونات مستوردة. 🇨🇳 3. مكونات من الصين: أشار تقرير لمنظمة Conflict Armament Research إلى محاولات الحوثيين استخدام قطع واردة من الصين في تطوير صواريخ باليستية متوسطة المدى، دون أن يعني ذلك تورط الحكومة الصينية. 🤖 4. الذكاء الاصطناعي: كشفت شركة Anthropic عن استخدام جهات مرتبطة بشمال اليمن أدواتها للمساعدة في مشروعات تسليحية، بينها صاروخ مخطط له بمدى يتجاوز 2,000 كيلومتر. 🛡️ 5. تحديات الدفاع الجوي: يرى خبراء أن اتساع مساحة السعودية واستنزاف مخزونات الصواريخ الاعتراضية خلال الحرب الإقليمية يزيدان صعوبة التصدي لجميع الهجمات. 🎯 6. الرد العسكري السعودي: أعلن التحالف تدمير 127 مخزنًا للأسلحة ومنصات إطلاق حوثية خلال عملياته الأخيرة. 💬 ولخّص خبير أمني الفكرة الأساسية: إيران لم تكتفِ بتسليح الحوثيين، بل ساعدتهم على تعلّم صناعة أسلحتهم. 🇸🇦 الخلاصة: يشير التقرير إلى أن التهديد الحوثي لم يعد يعتمد فقط على شحنات السلاح الإيراني المباشرة، بل على شبكة تصنيع وتوريد وخبرات تراكمت خلال سنوات. 📌 المصدر: رويترز — نقلًا عن خبراء عسكريين وأمنيين وتقارير بحثية.

story-33d9d246509e41ff63fb5d4a.content: NEW: Israel bans fiber-optic and SIM-controlled drones from civilian airspace for six months amid escalating drone threats. Defense Minister Katz is expected to sign the directive following Security Cabinet approval. The ban specifically targets drones controlled via fiber-optic cables — which are immune to electronic jamming — and those operating over cellular networks via SIM cards. The move comes after fiber-optic FPV drones, a tactic refined in Ukraine and adopted by Hezbollah, have proven extremely difficult to counter — flying too low for radar, resistant to jamming, and hard to intercept. Concerns also extend to potential use from the West Bank or against senior officials. Security forces and Civil Aviation Authority-approved operations are exempt. The temporary ban aims to reduce the “noise” of civilian drones so hostile ones are easier to detect while longer-term countermeasures (lasers, AI targeting, kinetic interceptors) are developed.

story-348179c3f9e11fa5f8aa54aa.content: في صيف 1914 لم يكن السؤال في أوروبا فقط: من يريد الحرب؟ كان هناك سؤال أخطر: من يستطيع أن ينتظر؟ كانت الجيوش المليونية تحتاج إلى تعبئة عبر شبكات السكك الحديدية وفق خطط أُعدّت مسبقًا بتفاصيل دقيقة. ومع تصاعد أزمة يوليو، تحولت التعبئة من إجراء عسكري إلى إشارة سياسية شديدة الخطورة. في 30 يوليو أمرت روسيا بالتعبئة العامة. وفي اليوم التالي أمهلت ألمانيا موسكو ساعات للتراجع عنها. السفير الأمريكي في برلين كتب يومها أن التعبئة الروسية، في تقديره، جعلت الحرب «حتمية». وبعد أيام كانت أوروبا في حرب عامة. المؤرخ A. J. P. Taylor سمّى ذلك لاحقًا «الحرب وفق جدول زمني»: خطط صُممت للردع والسرعة أصبحت، عند اندلاع الأزمة، تضغط على السياسيين كي يتحركوا قبل الخصم. لكن التاريخ يحتاج إلى دقة: القطارات لم تُشعل الحرب وحدها. القرارات السياسية سبقتها. ما فعلته خطط التعبئة الجامدة هو أنها ضيّقت الوقت والخيارات بعد بدء التصعيد؛ وهذا هو التفسير الأكثر حذرًا الذي تؤكده الدراسات اللاحقة. وهنا تصبح 1914 قصة معاصرة جدًا. الجيوش اليوم تطارد شيئًا واحدًا: تقليل زمن القرار. في مايو 2026 أعلن حلف الناتو مشروعًا يستهدف خفض الزمن بين وصول المعلومة واتخاذ القرار العسكري بأكثر من 50%، باستخدام تكامل البيانات والذكاء الاصطناعي. وفي الاتجاه المقابل يحذر معهد SIPRI من أن الذكاء الاصطناعي قد يضغط زمن القرار في الأزمات النووية ويزيد احتمالات سوء التقدير. المفارقة واضحة: السرعة تمنحك أفضلية عسكرية، لكنها قد تسلبك وقت التفكير السياسي. وفي منطقة مثل الشرق الأوسط، حيث تتقارب القواعد والجبهات ومنظومات الصواريخ والمسيّرات، يصبح السؤال في أي أزمة مقبلة ليس فقط: من يملك السلاح الأقوى؟ بل: من يملك وقتًا أطول ليتأكد أنه فهم ما يحدث قبل أن يضطر إلى الرد؟ فأحيانًا لا تبدأ الحروب لأن أحدًا اختارها كاملة؛ بل لأن كل طرف خشي أن يصبح الانتظار أخطر من الحركة.

story-351906d6051afb6e5b9b3a7e.content: NORTH KOREA | New Yalu River Bridge appears close to opening Commercial satellite imagery from September 28 shows growing activity at the new Sinuiju–Dandong border crossing between North Korea and China. Around 16 trucks appeared inside the North Korean customs complex between two satellite passes taken only hours apart, while smaller vehicles were visible near the Chinese customs facilities. Construction on both sides of the New Yalu River Bridge is now essentially complete. The crossing has remained unopened since the bridge itself was finished in 2014. Once operational, it is expected to become the main road-cargo route between China and North Korea, replacing much of the traffic currently handled by the older Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge. The latest activity suggests final preparations may now be underway ahead of a possible opening. Imagery: Planet Labs Date: September 28, 2026

story-389b966ef66f55116bd4fc27.content: 🇺🇸🇷🇺 US and Russia strip AI safeguards from UN autonomous weapons text – Washington Post The US and Russia pushed through the removal of key restrictions on the military use of AI from a UN draft on lethal autonomous weapons, The Washington Post reports, citing negotiation participants and documents it reviewed. At the Geneva talks, the delegations reportedly removed: ➡️the requirement that a human review AI-selected targets before a strike; ➡️provisions requiring ethical considerations; ➡️language requiring such systems to operate "predictably" and "reliably." According to WaPo, on the final day of talks the American and Russian delegations spent about 15 hours reworking the document. Each fielded a team of roughly ten lawyers, almost twice the size of other delegations. The talks are part of a UN effort to set international rules for lethal autonomous systems that can select and engage targets on their own. The agreed text is non-binding. Countries will meet again in Geneva in November to decide whether to open negotiations on a full international treaty. More than 70 states back the text as a basis for binding rules, but the process runs on consensus. Washington and Moscow both oppose legally binding limits, so they can effectively block it. The technology is already in use. In March, WaPo reported that the US military relied on Anthropic's Claude, integrated into Palantir's Maven Smart System, to suggest and prioritize targets and generate coordinates as it struck around 1,000 targets in the first 24 hours of the war on Iran.

story-39233f3388b9706ec4d4dd1d.content: 🇷🇺 🇺🇸 Russia and the US have reportedly secured the removal of several key restrictions on the use of military AI from a draft UN document on autonomous weapons. The negotiations took place in Geneva from August 31 to September 4 within the UN Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS). According to The Washington Post, Russian and US representatives removed proposed requirements that AI-powered weapons operate in a “predictable” and “reliable” manner, as well as provisions concerning ethical considerations in the use of such systems. The draft also no longer includes a requirement for mandatory human verification of targets selected by AI before a strike is carried out. The document agreed upon so far is not legally binding. What does this mean? “Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems” (LAWS) refers to weapons that can use software and AI to identify, select and potentially engage targets with limited or no direct human intervention. The central debate is about how much control humans should retain when AI is involved in decisions that could result in someone being killed. Supporters of strict regulation argue that humans should remain responsible for critical decisions, particularly target selection and the use of lethal force. Others focus on the military potential of autonomous systems and argue that excessive restrictions could limit technological development and military capabilities. The UN discussions are part of a broader international effort to determine whether and how such weapons should be regulated. @RusEvi_Ankara #Russia #USA #AI #AutonomousWeapons

story-3a3e681fc485714d4013ad86.content: Saudi technology company Echelon (@echelon__x) and U.S. autonomy software developer Applied Intuition (@AppliedInt) have partnered to bring physical AI technology to Saudi Arabia, with potential applications across trucking, ports, mining, manufacturing, agriculture, construction and robotaxis. Applied Intuition will provide the software and infrastructure for autonomous machines, while Riyadh-based Echelon will focus on local development, customization and integration with customers’ existing systems. Qasar Younis, co-founder and CEO of Applied Intuition, said: “Saudi Arabia is making one of the world's biggest investments in physical AI.” Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, Echelon’s founder and managing director, added: “Saudi Arabia has an opportunity not simply to adopt physical AI, but to help define how it is deployed at national scale.” Applied Intuition is also building a team in Riyadh, while the companies plan to develop Saudi engineering talent and explore how the technology can be deployed across priority industries. The agreement follows a separate collaboration between Applied Intuition and @HUMAIN targeting thousands of autonomous trucks along key Saudi freight corridors by 2030. story-3a787ac09d5d65e49b50a7fa.content: The main risk if a smart TV or similar IoT box got infected by such an AI worm is that it becomes part of a slow-spreading, hard-to-kill botnet. The device would run AI inference (using its limited CPU/RAM), which could slow normal functions, raise power use and heat, and generate unusual network traffic. Privacy exposure is possible if the box has a mic or camera, or if the worm pivots to other home devices. Removal might require a factory reset or replacement, since cheap unpatched hardware often lacks reliable updates. Spread would take days per copy and produce detectable multi-gigabyte transfers, but there is no central kill switch. This remains a controlled lab demonstration of near-future capability, not an active threat today.

story-3aab398a4a1e814a2b695749.content: الموجز اليومي 26 سبتمبر 2026 1. العلاقات الخليجية الأميركية: واشنطن وبكين ترفضان فرض رسوم على الممرات الدولية الخبر: أعلن البيت الأبيض اتفاق ترامب وشي على رفض فرض أي دولة أو جهة رسوما على الممرات الدولية، وعلى منع إيران من امتلاك سلاح نووي. كما أنشأ الطرفان حوارا وخط اتصال بشأن مخاطر الذكاء الاصطناعي. الدلالة: الاتفاق يستهدف مباشرة محاولة إيران التحكم في الملاحة أو فرض رسوم في هرمز، ويضع الصين أمام مسؤولية أكبر باعتبارها شريكا اقتصاديا رئيسيا لطهران وأكبر مشتر للطاقة الخليجية. التحليل: القيمة الحقيقية لن تقاس بالبيان، بل بمدى استخدام بكين نفوذها لإعادة الملاحة الحرة وتقليص الدعم الاقتصادي الذي يصل إلى إيران. كما قد يؤثر الحوار التقني الجديد في وصول الخليج إلى الرقائق والشراكات الأميركية والصينية. 2. إيران تنتظر الرد الأميركي على مقترح السبعة أيام الخبر: قدمت إيران عبر قطر مقترحا لإعادة فتح هرمز ووقف القتال خلال سبعة أيام، مقابل رفع الحصار الأميركي والإفراج عن أموال مجمدة ومنح إعفاءات لصادرات النفط. ولا تزال طهران ترفض التنازل عن التخصيب أو إخراج اليورانيوم عالي التخصيب. لم يتأكد رسميا أن ترامب رفض المقترح. الدلالة: المقترح يربط أمن الملاحة بتسوية أوسع مع واشنطن، لكنه يطلب تنازلات أميركية كبيرة دون تنازل نووي مماثل. التحليل: الاتفاق المؤقت قد يخفض النفط وتكاليف الشحن، لكن فشله قد يعيد الضربات الأميركية والتصعيد الإيراني ضد الملاحة الخليجية. 3. السعودية تعترض هجوما حوثيا جديدا الخبر: أعلن التحالف اعتراض صاروخين باليستيين باتجاه خميس مشيط ومسيرتين باتجاه الرياض. وسبق ذلك اجتماع مسؤولين عسكريين من السعودية وباكستان وتركيا لبحث التهديدات والتنسيق العسكري. لا يوجد تأكيد على مشاركة قوات أجنبية في عمليات الاعتراض. الدلالة: الحوثيون قادرون على مواصلة الضغط على الجنوب والعاصمة في وقت واحد، بينما بدأت السعودية تحويل علاقاتها الدفاعية الجديدة إلى تنسيق أكثر تنظيما. التحليل: الاختبار المقبل هو ما إذا كانت تركيا وباكستان ستقدمان أنظمة دفاع ومعلومات ودعما لوجستيا، أم سيبقى التعاون في حدود التخطيط السياسي والعسكري. 4. الضربات الروسية توقف أكبر مصنع للصلب في أوكرانيا الخبر: أوقفت أرسيلورميتال العمل في مصنع كريفي ريه بعد ضربات روسية متكررة، وقدرت خسائر خفض قيمة الأصول بنحو مليار دولار. كما قتلت هجمات على كييف سبعة أشخاص وأصابت 58. الدلالة: روسيا تستهدف قدرة أوكرانيا الاقتصادية والمالية على استمرار الحرب، وليس مواقعها العسكرية فقط. التحليل: تعطيل المصانع والموانئ سيزيد عجز الموازنة الأوكرانية واعتماد كييف على التمويل الغربي، مع تأثير محتمل في إمدادات الصلب وتكاليف الإعمار. 5. تسريب بيانات عبر وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي الخبر: كشفت OpenAI أن وكلاء آليين سربوا 53 صورة لمستخدمين، فيما قال رئيس لجنة التجارة الفيدرالية إن المسؤولية القانونية عن أخطاء الوكلاء يجب أن تبقى على الشركات والمطورين. تصريحاته توجه رقابي وليست قاعدة ملزمة جديدة. الدلالة: النقاش ينتقل من قدرات الوكلاء إلى مسؤولية الشركات عن تصرفاتهم وتسرب البيانات الناتج عنها. التحليل: الجهات السعودية والخليجية التي تستخدم الوكلاء في الحكومة والصحة والبنوك والبنية التحتية تحتاج إلى صلاحيات محدودة، وسجلات تدقيق، وإبلاغ إلزامي عن الحوادث، وتحديد واضح للمسؤولية مع مزودي التقنية. ما نتابع الرد الأميركي الرسمي على المقترح الإيراني، تنفيذ الصين لتعهداتها بشأن هرمز، الهجمات الحوثية وطبيعة الدعم التركي والباكستاني للسعودية، حركة الناقلات وأسعار التأمين، الضربات الروسية على الصناعة الأوكرانية، وأي إجراءات رقابية بعد تسريب بيانات وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي فاصل
